scenes.title: Seven days
scenes.narration: This is our last barrel. Seven days of food for eight people. Out there, the sea is full of cod, and the storm will not let us reach it. My best cow can barely stand. My name is Ketil. You call my people Vikings. And I am going to show you exactly how we survive seven months of winter.

scenes.title: Winternights
scenes.narration: Five months earlier. Winternights, the middle of October, when our year turns from summer to winter. Up here, in the far north of Norway, nothing will grow again until May. Seven months! Whatever we eat before then, we must gather now. Every fish, every sheep, every handful of barley. And one wrong guess, just one, means hunger in March.

scenes.title: Steinvik
scenes.narration: This is my farm, Steinvik. One longhouse of stone, timber and turf, a byre, a boathouse by the shore and the mountains behind us like a wall. We are five: my wife Ragnhild, my son Eyvind, my little Tora, and my old father Ulf, who has seen more winters than anyone on this island. And our animals. They matter more than you think.

scenes.title: The longhouse
scenes.narration: Inside, everything turns around the long hearth, a fire that runs down the middle of the floor. There is no chimney! Only a hole in the roof for the smoke. We sit, work and sleep on wide benches along the walls. And at the far end, behind a wooden wall the cows. Their bodies warm the whole house, all winter long.

scenes.title: Counting the hay
scenes.narration: But here is the question that decides everything: how much hay do we have? A cow eats a mountain of it before spring. So each autumn, my father climbs into the hay loft and counts, the way his father did. He measures with his arms and does the sums in his head. Then he tells me how many animals can live.

scenes.title: A bad summer
scenes.narration: This year he climbs down slowly. And he says nothing for a long time. The summer was wet. It rained for weeks while the grass lay cut in the fields, and half of the hay turned black and rotten. 'Ketil,' he says. 'We have hay for four cows. Not six.' And that is how my winter truly began.

scenes.title: The choice
scenes.narration: So we do what every farm in the north must do. We choose. Two cows, the old ram, and most of the pigs will not see the spring. It is hard. Tora cries for the little brown calf. But an animal that starves in March gives us nothing. An animal killed now, gives us meat for the whole winter.

scenes.title: Nothing wasted
scenes.narration: And nothing is wasted. Meat is smoked above the fire, or dried in the wind. Blood becomes sausage. Fat becomes tallow. Bones are boiled for soup; hides become shoes and blankets. Even the horns become cups! Ragnhild packs meat into barrels of sour whey, it keeps for months, without salt. And salt, up here is precious.

scenes.title: The feast
scenes.narration: Then comes the feast! With so much fresh meat, this is the one night of the year when everyone eats until they cannot move. We raise horns of ale to the gods, and to the dead of our family. My father tells the old stories. For one night nobody counts. Tomorrow, every mouthful will be counted again.

scenes.title: Stockfish
scenes.narration: But meat alone will not carry us to May. Our real treasure is this: stockfish. Cod, split and hung on wooden racks in the cold sea wind until it is dry and hard as a plank. It needs no salt at all. Kept dry, it lasts for years. Before we eat it, we beat it with a stone hammer, for a very, very long time.

scenes.title: The storehouse
scenes.narration: Our storehouse is dark and cool, and kept dry. Inside: stockfish tied in bundles, barley in sacks, tubs of butter, dried mutton, cheese, and berries dried in the sun. Every evening, I walk through it and I count. Then I count it again. It must be enough. It has to be.

scenes.title: Leaves and seaweed
scenes.narration: And the hay? We stretch it. All autumn, Eyvind and I cut leafy branches from the birch and the elm, and dry them in bundles for the animals. At low tide, the sheep walk down to the shore and eat seaweed. And when we clean fish, the heads and bones are boiled into a soup for the cows. Yes. Our cows eat fish!

scenes.title: Light in the dark
scenes.narration: By November, the days grow short. Very short. Soon the sun will disappear completely, for more than a month. So we make our own light. The livers of the cod are pressed into oil, and that oil burns in little stone lamps. The whole house smells of fish but it glows. And by that glow, Ragnhild weaves, and I mend nets.

scenes.title: Fire across the bay
scenes.narration: Then, one night in December, Eyvind runs in from the byre. 'Father! Look, there's fire across the bay!' Far away, on the other shore, a red glow is rising into the dark. That is Grim's farm. Our nearest neighbour. In winter, a fire does not just burn a house. It burns the food. It burns the hay. It burns everything.

scenes.title: Nothing left
scenes.narration: I strap on my skis and go along the shore in the dark. When I get there, the longhouse is already falling in. Grim is standing in the snow with his wife Asa and their baby, wrapped in one cloak. They saved their lives and nothing else. No food. No hay. Two sheep. That is all they have left.

scenes.title: The law of the guest
scenes.narration: An old saying among us: 'Fire is needed by the one who comes in with frozen knees.' No one turns a guest away in winter. Not ever. So now we are eight. Eight mouths, same food.

scenes.title: New rules
scenes.narration: So Ragnhild and I make new rules. Two meals a day, not three. Porridge in the morning, thinner than before. Fish and a little meat in the evening. Grim goes fishing with me whenever the sea allows it; every cod we catch now is one more day we buy. And Asa? She turns out to be the best weaver on the island!

scenes.title: The long dark
scenes.narration: Then the sun disappears. For weeks there is no daylight at all, only a blue glow at midday, and then darkness again. Some people go strange in the long dark. They stop talking. They stop getting up. So we keep busy: stories, songs, board games by the lamp. Anything to keep our minds away from the storehouse.

scenes.title: Yule
scenes.narration: And in the deepest dark comes Yule! We brew ale from barley saved all year, and we eat the best of what is left. We drink to a good year, and to the return of the sun. For three nights, the house is loud and warm. And Tora falls asleep in the middle of the table, with a piece of bread still in her hand.

scenes.title: The sun returns
scenes.narration: In the middle of January, we all climb the hill behind the farm and we wait. And then, a thin line of gold touches the tops of the mountains. The sun is back! Tora shouts and dances in the snow. My father closes his eyes and smiles. We made it through the dark. But the hardest part of winter is still ahead.

scenes.title: The storms
scenes.narration: February. Every winter, the cod come, huge shoals of them, to spawn along our coast. This is when we should fill our boats. But this year, the storms will not stop. Day after day, the wind screams, and the waves hit the rocks as high as a house. No boat can go out. And inside. I open the last barrel.

scenes.title: Huppa
scenes.narration: The hay is gone too. The cows eat leaves, seaweed, fish soup, and it is not enough. Huppa, our best milking cow, can hardly stand anymore. If she dies, we lose our milk, our butter, our cheese for the whole next year. Every morning I go into the byre, afraid of what I will find.

scenes.title: The empty barrel
scenes.narration: On the seventh day of storm, Grim comes to me. 'Ketil, the wind is dropping. Let's go. Now.' The sea is still wild. My father says it is madness. Ragnhild says nothing she just looks at the children. I look at the empty barrel. And I pick up my oars.

scenes.title: Into the sea
scenes.narration: We row out in the grey dawn, Grim, Eyvind and me. The waves lift our little boat like a leaf and drop it again. My hands are frozen to the oars. Eyvind bails water as if his life depends on it, because it does. And then, at last, we reach the fishing ground and let our lines down into the black water.

scenes.title: The cod
scenes.narration: Nothing. Nothing and then, a tug. And another! The line almost pulls Eyvind into the sea! Cod! Big ones, as long as my arm! The shoal is right under us. We pull, and pull, until the boat is so heavy the water almost comes over the side. Grim is laughing like a madman. And we row home singing.

scenes.title: Home
scenes.narration: The whole family is waiting on the shore. Ragnhild runs into the icy water up to her knees! That night, we eat fresh cod boiled with the last of the butter, the best meal of my life. Huppa gets a whole bucket of fish soup. And in the morning she is standing up.

scenes.title: Carrying the cows
scenes.narration: In May, the snow finally melts from the fields, and the first green grass appears. After seven months inside, our cows are so weak they can barely walk. So we do what our grandfathers did: we carry them out to the grass. Yes, we carry them! And when Huppa tastes that first grass she runs.

scenes.title: How we survived
scenes.narration: So how did we survive seven months of winter? We counted the hay. Dried and smoked everything. Fed our cows fish! Burned cod oil for light shared our fire. And when it mattered, we took our chances with the sea.

scenes.title: A new house
scenes.narration: That summer, we all helped Grim build a new longhouse: stone, timber and turf. When it was finished, Asa gave us the finest cloak she had ever woven. My name is Ketil of Steinvik and that was the winter of eight hundred and seventy-two. But mine was not the only hard winter in history.

scenes.narration: Almost a thousand years after me, a young soldier marches toward Moscow with Napoleon's army, six hundred thousand men. Winter is coming. Very few of them will ever come home. How did he survive? That story is next. And here, the fire is still burning.
